title: Casablanca opens in New York

facts.text: On Thanksgiving Day, 26 November 1942, Warner Bros. opened Casablanca at its Hollywood Theatre in New York City.
The studio had planned to release it in June 1943. Then, on 8 November 1942, American and British troops landed in French North Africa, including at Casablanca itself.
Warner moved the New York premiere up to catch the headlines, only eighteen days after the landings.

Humphrey Bogart played Rick Blaine, an American running a nightclub in Vichy controlled Casablanca, and Ingrid Bergman played Ilsa Lund, the woman who walks back into his life with her husband, a Resistance leader.
The story came from an unproduced play, Everybody Comes to Rick's, by Murray Burnett and Joan Alison. Producer Hal Wallis bought the rights in January 1942 for $20,000.
The general release followed on 23 January 1943, while Roosevelt and Churchill were meeting at Casablanca. It seemed as though the President himself was promoting the film.
The Office of War Information kept the film from troops in North Africa, fearing it would anger Vichy supporters there.
The film cost about $1,039,000 and earned $3.7 million in its first American run. The Hollywood Theatre alone took in $255,000 in ten weeks.

It won three Oscars, Best Picture, Best Director for Michael Curtiz and Best Screenplay. When Best Picture was announced, Jack Warner rushed to the stage ahead of Wallis, who left the studio soon after.
Many extras in the scene where the cafe drowns out German officers with La Marseillaise were real European refugees, and a witness said they were crying.

declassified.fact: Two of the actors had fled the Nazis themselves. Marcel Dalio, who played the croupier, and Madeleine LeBeau, who played Yvonne, reached Hollywood with seventeen dollars and no English between them.

body:
Warner Bros. had planned to hold Casablanca until June 1943. Then Allied troops landed at Casablanca, and the studio moved fast.

26 November 1942. On Thanksgiving Day the film opened at the Hollywood Theatre in New York, just eighteen days after American and British troops came ashore in French North Africa. Humphrey Bogart played Rick Blaine, running a nightclub in Vichy controlled Casablanca.

The luck held. The general release came on 23 January 1943, while Roosevelt and Churchill were meeting in Casablanca itself. Many of the extras who sang La Marseillaise in the cafe were real European refugees, and a witness said they were crying.
